As written, the condition `end > workingHour.endTime` will never be true (unless slotStartTime itself is past the end), so slots that start within working hours but extend beyond the working window will not be filtered out. findings.title: Double filtering of date overrides can incorrectly remove valid slots
findings.body: getTimeSlots already accounts for date overrides and working hours when generating timeSlots. Then in availableTimeSlots.filter for fixed hosts, checkIfIsAvailable is called again with the raw dateOverrides and workingHours. This double-processing, combined with the flawed date override logic in checkIfIsAvailable, can cause valid slots to be rejected. For example, a fixed host with an override that is correctly handled by getTimeSlots may be marked unavailable by checkIfIsAvailable due to offset or comparison errors. This directly undermines the PR's goal of respecting fixed host overrides in round-robin events.

findings.title: Working hours check uses slot start time for both start and end
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, the lines `const start = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` and `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` use the same value for start and end. The end should likely be computed from slotEndTime. As written, the condition `end > workingHour.endTime` will never be true (unless slotStartTime itself is past the end), so slots that start within working hours but extend beyond the working window will not be filtered out. This check is redundant because buildSlots already ensures slots fit, but the incorrect computation may hide logical errors or cause unexpected behavior if working hours are ever used independently.

findings.title: Date override logic fails when multiple overrides exist for the same date
findings.body: The checkIfIsAvailable function uses a `find` on dateOverrides and returns false if the callback returns true for any override. If there are multiple overrides for the same date, the callback may return true for an override where the slot is outside, causing the entire slot to be considered unavailable, even if another override for the same date would have allowed it. This can lead to false negatives in availability for users with more than one override on a given day.

findings.title: Date override conversion ignores day shift when offset crosses midnight
findings.body: The calculation `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute").hour() * 60 + ...` extracts only the hour and minute from the shifted UTC time, discarding the date component. If the timezone offset difference causes the shifted time to cross midnight (e.g., an override at 23:00 in one timezone appearing as 01:00 the next day in the invitee's timezone), the resulting slot will be placed at 1:00 AM on the same invitee day rather than the next day. This can cause overrides near day boundaries to produce incorrect availability.

findings.title: No test for round-robin fixed host date override scenario
findings.body: The PR's main goal is to ensure date overrides of fixed hosts are respected in round-robin events, but the only new test is for a single-user event. There is no test with a round-robin event containing a fixed host with an override and a non-fixed host available. This leaves the critical double-filtering path untested and could allow regressions in the exact scenario the PR is meant to fix.
